sections.heading: C — Fitness to drive
sections.markdown:
## C — Fitness to drive

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A20
Safe driving depends on clear sight, alertness, freedom from alcohol or drug impairment, health and emotional readiness. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A20
Poor vision makes it harder to detect road conditions and respond to danger promptly. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A20
Kansas requires a successful vision test before issuing a driver license. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A20
The vision standard is at least 20/40 in one eye, using corrective lenses if needed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A20
A corrective-lens license restriction requires the driver to wear glasses or contacts while driving. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A20
Get regular eye examinations because deteriorating vision may otherwise go unnoticed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A20
A corrective-lens requirement applies even to a short local drive. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A20
Keep spare corrective lenses in the vehicle in case the usual pair is damaged or lost. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A20
Avoid tinted lenses at night because they reduce the light available for seeing. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A20
Horns, sirens and skidding-tire sounds can warn a driver about danger. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A20
A change in tire noise may signal a changed road surface or tire condition. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A20
Engine sounds can provide clues about how the engine is operating. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A20
Hearing loss can develop gradually without being noticed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A20
Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness caused by factors such as strain, repetition, illness or insufficient sleep. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A20
Fatigue weakens vision and judgment. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A20
Fatigue can distort judgments about speed and distance. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A20
A fatigued driver may take longer to decide and become irritated more easily. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A20
Fatigue increases crash risk and may lead to falling asleep while driving. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A21
Most adults need 7 to 9 hours of sleep to stay properly alert during the day. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A21
On a long trip, plan a rest break about every 100 miles or every 2 hours. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A21
A travel companion can provide conversation and share driving duties. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A21
Before a trip, avoid alcohol and medicines that cause sedation. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A21
Check medicine labels or ask a doctor about sedating effects before driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A21
Needing loud radio sound or an open window to remain awake is a fatigue warning. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A21
Trouble keeping the eyes open is a fatigue warning. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A21
Drifting out of the lane is a fatigue warning. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A21
When fatigued, stop driving and use an exit, rest area or overnight sleeping place. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A21
The handbook recommends a 15-to-20-minute nap in a safe parking place when sleepy. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A21
The handbook says caffeine comparable to 2 cups of coffee can temporarily improve alertness. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A21
Caffeine wears off and must not be relied on to prevent fatigue. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A21
The handbook suggests having caffeine, followed by a brief nap, to gain benefits from both. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A21
Try to avoid late-night driving between midnight and 6 a.m. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A21
Sleep is the best prevention for fatigue. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A21
A distraction is anything that draws attention away from operating the vehicle. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A21
A mental distraction can be dangerous even while the driver's eyes face the road. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A21
Using a phone, navigation system or other electronic device can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A21
Changing audio or climate settings while moving can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A21
Grooming, eating, drinking or smoking can divert driving attention. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A21
Conversations and attending to children or pets can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A21
Reading maps or other material can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A21
Reaching for a dropped object can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A21
Watching a roadside crash or traffic stop can divert attention from driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A21
Sunlight or a sunset can become an outside distraction. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

Misconceptions: Coffee or a cold shower does not remove alcohol from the bloodstream; feeling more alert must not be treated as sober driving ability.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: sight, sleep, attention, substances, health and emotion; these words retrieve the cited fitness checks.
Glossary: Fatigue is physical or mental tiredness; distraction takes attention from driving; the BAC definition appears in a fact block.
Dynamic facts: Legal sanctions and test-refusal rules are revision-bound and require issuer refresh; undated crash statistics and fixed sober-up calculations are isolated as debt.

sections.heading: C — Fitness to drive
sections.markdown:
## C — Fitness to drive

FACT_ID: sec03-F44 | anchor: A21
People or objects in the roadway, as well as road construction, can divert attention from driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F45 | anchor: A21
Reading billboards or roadside advertisements can distract a driver. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec03-F46 | anchor: A22
Park safely before using a cell phone. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F47 | anchor: A22
Avoid arguments and stressful conversations that compete with attention to the road. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F48 | anchor: A22
Allow time to stop for food instead of eating while driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F49 | anchor: A22
Secure children properly and give them suitable activities before traveling. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F50 | anchor: A22
Secure pets in a carrier or portable kennel before moving the vehicle. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F51 | anchor: A22
Set vehicle controls before departure, at normal stops or with a passenger's help. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F52 | anchor: A22
Keep attention on the immediate travel path rather than distant distractions. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F53 | anchor: A22
Plan the route and review maps before driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F54 | anchor: A22
If a map must be checked during a trip, first park in a safe place. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F55 | anchor: A22
Do not converse with friends in another vehicle while driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F56 | anchor: A22
Do not wear music headphones while driving. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F57 | anchor: A22
The driver remains responsible for safe vehicle operation when a distraction contributes to a crash. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec03-F58 | anchor: A21
The handbook advises avoiding excessive caffeine when responding to fatigue. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0021]
